entries.title: Right now
entries.detail: Sampled once a second while this page is open. Memory counts what is not available: the page cache is reclaimable and doesn't count.

entries.title: Displays
entries.detail: Counts the screens Hyprland has switched on. The Displays page also lists connected screens that are turned off.

entries.title: Your palette
entries.detail: Sixteen slots. Everything in the shell is drawn from these. Point at one to read its value.

entries.title: Lock while playing
entries.detail: Album colours hold until playback stops

entries.title: Tint media cards
entries.detail: Works on its own: the media cards take the cover's colours even when the shell doesn't follow the album.

entries.title: Looks
entries.detail: A look is the bar, the sidebar, the style settings and your current colours in one .json file. No wallpaper, no paths, nothing personal, and never your motion settings. Import shows what it would change first, and you can undo it.

entries.title: Classics
entries.detail: Well-known schemes set up for the shell, each with the light and dark version its makers drew where there is one. Choosing one holds it through wallpaper changes; the wallpaper's own colours let go of it.

entries.title: Yours
entries.detail: Schemes you saved from the Colours panel, which is also where you make one: pick the sixteen colours, then save.

entries.title: Inner pill
entries.detail: Off sits this module directly on the group's own pill instead of the lighter shared chip.

entries.title: Hero
entries.detail: Puts this module on a tinted chip in your accent: the surface's one emphasised pill, as a desktop widget's hero. Each surface has one.

entries.title: Group spacing
entries.detail: Distance between icons in this group: %1.

entries.title: Size
entries.detail: How much room this takes, in pixels. With a module to follow, this is the part that doesn't change.

entries.title: When it grows
entries.detail: Grow adds the module's width to the size. Fill takes it away from the size, never below nothing, so the module and the spacer together stay as wide as the size.

entries.title: Only while Do Not Disturb
entries.detail: Hides the bell unless Do Not Disturb is on, so it reads as a discreet indicator rather than a permanent icon.

entries.title: Always on
entries.detail: Hides notifications and the overview from screen capture even when nothing is streaming. The pill's click still pauses it.

entries.title: Panel header
entries.detail: The title row at the top of this module's panel. Off, the panel opens straight onto its content and is a little shorter.

entries.title: Peek
entries.detail: When something happens to it, a card opens beside it for a moment, on the monitor you're on and never over a panel you opened.

entries.title: Peek is set on the Clips page
Apps
entries.detail: Click an app to open it or go to its next window; Shift-click for a new one; middle-click closes its newest window. Right-click for its jump list. Super+T puts the keyboard on the dock; Super+Alt+1–9 opens its nth app.

entries.title: Start button
entries.detail: The app launcher, at the start of the dock. Without it, the launcher keybind (Super+R by default) still opens it.

entries.title: Downloads
entries.detail: At the dock's end. Click it for your newest files.

entries.title: Trash
entries.detail: At the dock's end. Drop files on it; right-click it to empty.

entries.title: Style
entries.detail: ii is End-4's dock: flat rounded buttons, up to three dots under an app (one per window), hairlines between groups, a keep button before the apps (when the sidebar auto-hides, it holds the dock out) and an overview button after them. It has no magnification.

entries.title: Dock inner pill
entries.detail: Running apps sit on a pill, neighbours sharing one, like the bar's workspaces.

entries.title: App slots
entries.detail: The sidebar's and the bar's dock always show this many app slots, with a dot for each one that is empty, so the dock never changes length and the modules next to it stay put. More apps than that scroll: use the wheel over the dock (Ctrl and the wheel is an app's own volume or windows). Off lets the dock grow with its apps.

entries.title: Icon tiles
entries.detail: On the sidebar's dock, every app icon sits on a tile of the same shape, so a round logo and a square one look like a set. The icons keep their colours.

entries.title: Previews
entries.detail: Hover an app for a live thumbnail of each of its windows.

entries.title: Peek
entries.detail: Rest on a window in a preview to glance at its workspace, with that window lit.

entries.title: Melting
entries.detail: Previews and the right-click menu melt out of the dock, inside its length, instead of floating above it.

entries.title: Cap
entries.detail: How much of the edge the dock may take before it scrolls.

entries.title: Temperatures
entries.detail: An inner arc on the CPU and GPU rings showing the temperature, 0–100°C.

entries.title: Split network
entries.detail: Download on the network ring's outer arc, upload on the inner one.

entries.title: Line speed
entries.detail: What a full network ring means. Fixed, so an idle link never looks busy.

entries.title: Readings
entries.detail: The button shows the first three

entries.title: Alerts
entries.detail: A ring held over its threshold says so in its card. CPU and memory alert on load, the temperatures on degrees.

entries.title: Library
entries.detail: Every module, by kind. Click one to see it above, press Add to put it where it belongs, or drag it onto the bar or the sidebar. Drop a module here to take it off.

entries.title: Size
entries.detail: Small, Normal and Big move the bar's thickness, roundness, inset and the text and icon scales together. Any slider takes you off them, to Custom. The sidebar's size is the dock's icon size, on the Sidebar page.

entries.title: Opacity
entries.detail: Translucency needs a compositor blur behind it. Hyprland's is in Desktop › Tuning.

entries.title: Text
entries.detail: How big the text runs: the clock, the workspace numbers, labels.

entries.title: Icons
entries.detail: How big the icons run. Separate from text: a glyph is an icon that happens to be a character.

entries.title: Sidebar
entries.detail: Each switch is on while the sidebar follows the bar's value. Turn one off to give the sidebar its own, starting from the bar's.

entries.title: Tooltips
entries.detail: Resting the pointer on a bar module shows its name and what it is doing right now: the network you are on, the volume, how many updates are waiting.

entries.title: Group pills
entries.detail: The bar's groups are always islands. The sidebar can run one pill down each region instead, with a divider between groups.

entries.title: Pills
entries.detail: The chips the modules stand on. A module can opt out of its inner pill in its own settings, in Modules.

entries.title: Anchor on workspaces
entries.detail: Keeps the workspace dots at the exact centre of the screen, however wide the modules either side of them grow.

entries.title: Presets
entries.detail: Both surfaces, saved under a name: what is on them and every knob on this page. A preset saved before the sidebar was in presets leaves the sidebar alone.

entries.title: Profile
entries.detail: Trades battery life against how hard the machine will work.

entries.title: Rest the shell
entries.detail: Rests the cava background, wallpaper effects, floating cookies and the beat clock, and caps Wallpaper Engine at 30 fps. Animations stay.

entries.title: No adapter
entries.detail: No Bluetooth adapter was found, or BlueZ isn't running.

entries.title: Discoverable
entries.detail: Others can find this machine.

entries.title: Accept pairing
entries.detail: Devices may start pairing.

entries.title: Announce connections
entries.detail: A card on connect and drop

entries.title: Low battery warnings
entries.detail: A notification at the threshold, and again at half of it, once each per charge.

entries.title: Battery ring on the bar
entries.detail: Lowest battery, around the icon

entries.title: Recorder
entries.detail: Clipping keeps a replay buffer running, across reloads and reboots, so Alt+F10 always has something to save.

entries.title: Screen
entries.detail: Which monitor is recorded

entries.title: Desktop audio
entries.detail: What you hear: the default output.

entries.title: Microphone
entries.detail: Your voice: the default input.

entries.title: Cursor
entries.detail: Draw the pointer into the video.

entries.title: Include
entries.detail: Besides the picture

entries.title: Separate tracks
entries.detail: On, the mic gets a track of its own, for editing. Players, browsers and Discord play only the first track, so export with Mixed audio to share.

entries.title: Capture
entries.detail: Focused follows whichever monitor you're on when it starts. Portal asks once through the desktop portal and remembers.

entries.title: A clip keeps
entries.detail: The newest part of the buffer

entries.title: Stored
entries.detail: Memory is the fastest. A temp file on disk spares RAM for a long buffer.

entries.title: Replay buffer
entries.detail: How far back a clip can reach. In quality mode its size follows what's on screen; bitrate mode fixes it.

entries.title: Quality
entries.detail: Constant quality stays sharp in motion and its size varies. A fixed bitrate gives a predictable file and buffer size.

entries.title: Peek
entries.detail: A saved clip opens a card beside the sidebar button for a moment, with its thumbnail.

entries.title: Notify
entries.detail: Also send a notification per saved clip, for when the sidebar is hidden.

entries.title: Name by game
entries.detail: Name a clip after the window you cut it in, so the library can group by game. A game under Steam, Proton

entries.title: Clip & record
entries.detail: Keep recording a few seconds after you press Clip it, so a play you only reacted to afterwards is in the clip.

entries.title: Remember the song
entries.detail: Stamp a saved clip with the song your media player was playing (Spotify included). It shows in the library and can be searched.

entries.title: Remember who was in the call
entries.detail: Stamp a saved clip with the names of the people in your Discord voice channel. The names are written to a file in your state folder; they are never sent anywhere.

entries.title: Share
entries.detail: Discord upload size and what a clip remembers

entries.title: Clean-up
entries.detail: Only when you press the button

entries.title: Look
entries.detail: The fill colour and the size. The outline is always the shell's background colour.

entries.title: Shake to find
entries.detail: Part of the motion plugin: a quick shake makes the pointer big for a moment, so you can find it.

entries.title: Motion effects
entries.detail: Tilt, rotate or stretch the pointer as it moves, with the hypr-dynamic-cursors plugin.

entries.title: Presets
entries.detail: Colour, size and motion tuning, saved under a name. Loading one never turns the cursor theme or the plugin on or off.

entries.title: Shown
entries.detail: How many pictures Personalize shows: the one on the desktop, then your newest. 0 hides them.

entries.title: Preview the menu
entries.detail: Opens it in the middle of the screen

entries.title: Quick settings
entries.detail: Up to six round switches. Switches stay open for the next one; one-offs close the menu.

entries.title: More options
entries.detail: Tap a place to list it under Show more options; the arrows set the order.

entries.title: Icon row
entries.detail: Up to six, along the top. A capture closes the menu; a recording stays.

entries.title: Sign-in
entries.detail: How the shell talks to Discord, so the sidebar's Voice module can mute, deafen and screen share.

entries.title: Re-read discord-rpc.json
entries.detail: Picks up a client id you added, without clearing a live card

entries.title: Use the AI title
entries.detail: Instead of the short session name

entries.title: Claude Code
entries.detail: Shows what you're doing in Claude Code as your Discord status. It needs a separate app you register, with a client id and nothing else.

entries.title: Your own application
entries.detail: About a minute, once

entries.title: Counter-Strike 2
entries.detail: Shows your match as your Discord status. No app to set up: it uses Valve's own.

entries.title: Screen share & camera
entries.detail: Discord has no RPC command for these, so the shell presses Discord's own keybind. Set the same combinations as Discord → Settings → Keybinds; screen share has no default.

entries.title: Forget everyone
entries.detail: Names and time only, on this computer

entries.title: Call log
entries.detail: Keeps how long you have been in a call with each person, for the Board tab of the voice panel. Names and time only, on this computer, until you forget them. No server or channel names, no record of when each call was. Discord doesn't say who your friends are, so it counts everyone who joined; hide anyone from the board there.

entries.title: Arrangement
entries.detail: Drag a screen to move it

entries.title: On
entries.detail: Turn a screen off without unplugging it. At least one has to stay on.

entries.title: Variable refresh rate
entries.detail: Adaptive sync (FreeSync / G-Sync compatible). Only on screens that support it.

entries.title: Panel
entries.detail: Tap a section to show it; the arrows set the order.

entries.title: Switches
entries.detail: Up to eight, shown in the order you pick them.

entries.title: Opens after
entries.detail: How long the pointer rests in the corner before the panel opens. Short is quick; longer keeps a pointer that is only passing through from opening it.

entries.title: Closes after
entries.detail: How long the pointer must be away from the panel before it goes. Longer forgives a slip off the edge.

entries.title: Size
entries.detail: The whole panel, text and icons together.

entries.title: Feel
entries.detail: Nothing opens while a fullscreen window is on that screen. A key opens it too: qs ipc call hotcorner toggle.

entries.title: Shape
entries.detail: Gaps, border, rounding, opacity

entries.title: Blur & shadow
entries.detail: Behind translucent windows

entries.title: Window wobble
entries.detail: Jelly while you drag

entries.title: Snap floating windows
entries.detail: SUPER-drag a floating window to an edge or corner to fill a half, a quarter or the screen.

entries.title: Snap windows to the widget grid
entries.detail: A floating window you SUPER-drag lands on the same grid as your desktop widgets (set in Desktop › Widgets). Dropping in a zone above still wins.

entries.title: Input
entries.detail: Focus and snapping

entries.title: Animations
entries.detail: Each animation's speed (lower is faster), and whether it runs at all.

entries.title: Opens on
entries.detail: Resting the pointer opens it after a moment; a click on the handle then keeps it open. With Click, only a click opens it, so a pointer passing along the bar never does.

entries.title: Opens after
entries.detail: How long the pointer rests on the handle before the card opens. Longer keeps a pointer that is only passing along the bar from opening it.

entries.title: Closes after
entries.detail: How long the pointer must be off the card before it goes. A pin keeps it open.

entries.title: Handle length
entries.detail: How long the handle is, on the bar's top edge. A longer one is easier to land on.

entries.title: Size
entries.detail: The whole card, text and icons together.

entries.title: Live handle
entries.detail: While a song plays or a timer runs, the middle island's handle hangs out of the bar as a small pill that says so, and the card grows out of it. A recording always shows, and a click on it stops the recording. An empty middle island has no handle and no pill.

entries.title: Handle
entries.detail: Where the middle island's handle sits, and what it shows at rest. The side islands' handles stand over the cards they open. Keys open it too: qs ipc call island toggle, or island show media.

entries.title: Settings window
entries.detail: Window: a floating window the compositor places, like any other app. Panel: pinned to the bottom edge and merged into the frame, so it never covers the bar.

entries.title: Resized panels
entries.detail: Drag a panel's outer bottom corner to resize it. Click one here to put it back to its default size.

entries.title: Panel backdrop
entries.detail: Soft cookie shapes drifting behind every panel. They hold still when animations are switched off, and cost nothing while no panel is open.

entries.title: Cookies on the bar, sidebar & frame
Your layouts
entries.detail: The bar's keyboard pill cycles these, in this order. To reorder, remove one and add it back, and it goes to the end. Saved to hardware.lua and applied now, so a Hyprland restart keeps them.

entries.title: Speed
entries.detail: Hyprland's sensitivity: 0 is the device's own speed.

entries.title: Acceleration
entries.detail: Adaptive speeds up with faster movement; Flat keeps it 1:1 (what most players want).

entries.title: Left-handed
entries.detail: Swaps the primary and secondary buttons.

entries.title: Mouse
entries.detail: Applies to every pointer. Saved to hardware.lua; Reload in the bar above applies it.

entries.title: Key repeat
entries.detail: What a held-down key does: how soon it starts repeating, and how fast.

entries.title: Natural scrolling
entries.detail: Content follows your fingers, like a phone.

entries.title: Tap and drag
entries.detail: Tap, then keep the finger down to drag.

entries.title: Ignore while typing
entries.detail: The touchpad pauses briefly after a key press, so a palm doesn't move the cursor.

entries.title: Two-finger right-click
entries.detail: Click with two fingers for a right-click and three for a middle-click, instead of by where you press.

entries.title: Touchpad
entries.detail: Laptop touchpads. Saved to hardware.lua; Reload in the bar above applies it.

entries.title: Automatic
entries.detail: Follows the system

entries.title: Shell language
entries.detail: The language of the shell's own text. Only strings that have been prepared for translation change; everything else stays in English. To add a language, copy translations/en_US.json to a new <code>.json and translate the right-hand sides.

entries.title: System locale
entries.detail: What the system reports right now. Picking a locale in the list sets the language, date and number formats programs start with. It needs your password, and running programs keep the old one until they restart.

entries.title: Temperature unit
entries.detail: Celsius or Fahrenheit for every temperature the weather shows.

entries.title: Weather location
entries.detail: Used by the weather widget, the clock panel, night light's sunset schedule and the greeter. Only the place you pick is ever requested; your location is never looked up from your IP.

entries.title: Prefixes
entries.detail: Typed into the launcher's empty field, a prefix switches its mode: > runs a command, ? asks, + installs a package, ; searches your clipboard, : finds an emoji. Sums, unit conversions and site shortcuts (yt cats) just work.

entries.title: Shell actions
entries.detail: Night light, game mode, the power menu and the rest of what the shell can do, as results when you type their name.

entries.title: Settings
entries.detail: Three letters or more also search Settings; picking one opens its page.

entries.title: Calculator
entries.detail: Sums and unit conversions answer in the launcher: 12*8, 10 km to mi.

entries.title: Learn from use
entries.detail: Apps you open often rise within equally good matches. Off, ranking is match quality alone and nothing new is remembered.

entries.title: Rows shown
entries.detail: How many results fit before the list scrolls. The card grows by a row each.

entries.title: Results
entries.detail: What it offers beside apps

entries.title: Model
entries.detail: Empty is the provider's default. Change it if a provider starts answering 404.

entries.title: Session
entries.detail: Kept between questions

entries.title: Search the web first
entries.detail: Gemini only. The question also reaches the search backend.

entries.title: Ask
entries.detail: Start a launcher line with ? to ask. Nothing is sent until you press Enter. Off, ? opens a web search in your browser instead.

entries.title: Search engine
entries.detail: The address a web search opens; %s is replaced by what you typed.

entries.title: Engine name
entries.detail: What the launcher calls it where it offers a search.

entries.title: History
entries.detail: Apps you open often rise within equally good matches. Only app ids and counts are kept, never what you typed.

entries.title: Run & search
entries.detail: > runs a command in a terminal. A search that finds no app offers the web search instead.

entries.title: Install with +
entries.detail: A line starting with + searches the repos and installs a package through the update runner.

entries.title: AUR lookups
entries.detail: The AUR half of + sends the longest word you typed to aur.archlinux.org, and only in + mode. Off keeps + to the repos synced on this machine.

entries.title: Clipboard with ;
entries.detail: A line starting with ; searches what you copied. Enter puts the entry back on the clipboard. Off, ; is just a semicolon.

entries.title: Prefix modes
entries.detail: Lines that start with a symbol

entries.title: Site shortcuts
entries.detail: Type a key, a space, then what to search

entries.title: Now playing
entries.detail: Bottom centre: the track, its cover and controls.

entries.title: Notifications
entries.detail: Right edge, with their full text, to anyone at the screen.

entries.title: System stats
entries.detail: Top centre.

entries.title: Calendar
entries.detail: Bottom left.

entries.title: Discord call
entries.detail: Top centre, while you're in a call.

entries.title: Session actions
entries.detail: Left edge: suspend, restart, log out. Log out discards unsaved work.

entries.title: Audio spectrum
entries.detail: Across the bottom.

entries.title: Lyrics on YouTube
entries.detail: Show lyrics under Now playing for YouTube videos too, not only music players.

entries.title: What it shows
entries.detail: Everything on the lock screen is readable by whoever is standing at the machine.

entries.title: PAM service
entries.detail: Press Enter to set it

entries.title: Authentication
entries.detail: Which PAM stack the password box asks. \"login\" exists everywhere. If the lock ever refuses a correct password: Ctrl+Alt+F2, log in, and run loginctl unlock-session.

entries.title: Animate the scene
entries.detail: Off holds one frame of the scene's preview, the only real cure for its short loop.

entries.title: Background
entries.detail: What sits behind the clock. A running Wallpaper Engine scene shows as its blurred preview: the renderer publishes no still of the live frame.

entries.title: Lock before sleep
entries.detail: Locks as the machine suspends or hibernates, so it wakes to the lock screen.

entries.title: Lock when idle
entries.detail: Leave this off until you've tested unlocking. The bar's idle pill and gamemode hold it off.

entries.title: Profile picture
entries.detail: Lock screen only. Nothing is written to ~/.face.

entries.title: Ripple between lines
entries.detail: When the card slides to the next line, the lines further from it arrive a little later, like a wave.

entries.title: Soft focus
entries.detail: Blurs the lines that are two or more away from the one being sung, more the further they are.

entries.title: Motion
entries.detail: How far each word travels as it is sung, never the timing, which stays keyed to the vocal. Point at the line to play it.

entries.title: Look up as a fallback
entries.detail: Asks NetEase and LRCLIB when the Spotify bridge has nothing. It sends the artist, title and album.

entries.title: Source
entries.detail: Which provider answered for the current track, and whether the shell may look lyrics up itself.

entries.title: Translation
entries.detail: Which service translates, and its optional API key.

entries.title: Radio blocked
entries.detail: A kill switch or function key holds Wi-Fi off

entries.title: Wi-Fi
entries.detail: Join, forget, or connect to a hidden network.

entries.title: Speed test
entries.detail: What the link can carry, measured only when you press Run. It contacts a third party and moves real data, so both are named under the trace.

entries.title: DNS
entries.detail: Which resolver answers your lookups. Changing it reconnects the link for a moment.

entries.title: Needs a backend
entries.detail: Install one, then reload the shell

entries.title: Temperature
entries.detail: Lower is warmer. 6500K is daylight, no change at all.

entries.title: Night is
entries.detail: Sunset to sunrise comes from your weather location. Without one, the fixed hours are used.

entries.title: Hours
entries.detail: From and until, as HH:MM. Crossing midnight (20:00 until 07:00) is the normal case.

entries.title: Turn on at night
entries.detail: Warms the screen only during the night hours. The switch above still has to be on.

entries.title: Only at night
entries.detail: Night light's hours, from its schedule or the sun, even while Night light itself is off.

entries.title: Anti-flashbang
entries.detail: A Hyprland screen shader, so it works without hyprsunset or gammastep. It measures the focused screen once a second.

entries.title: This week
entries.detail: App names and minutes, kept on this computer only, never window titles.

entries.title: Away after
entries.detail: With no input for this long, you count as away and the clock stops.

entries.title: Daily goal
entries.detail: A limit for the day, in hours. The panel draws a ring round today's card toward it and counts the days you stayed under. Off: no ring, and the run is just days in a row.

entries.title: What counts
entries.detail: The focused window's app counts while you're at the machine. Idle time doesn't, unless something keeps the screen awake (a video playing). Locked time never does.

entries.title: Keep
entries.detail: Days older than this are dropped.

entries.title: Set up
entries.detail: Packages, the morphing plugin, Hyprland wiring, app theming and the optional extras. Tick what you want and press the one button. The same thing the first-run window shows.

entries.title: Hyprland
entries.detail: How Hyprland is wired and who owns the notifications. Tap one that needs attention for its fix.

entries.title: Tools
entries.detail: Optional tools. Each feature that needs one is switched off with a reason until it is installed. Tap one for the command.

entries.title: Spotify lyrics
entries.detail: The bridge that lets the shell read what Spotify is playing, for lyrics.

entries.title: Accounts
entries.detail: Where API keys and the Discord client secret are kept.

entries.title: Password prompts
entries.detail: When pkexec or an app asks for your password, the dialog is the shell's own instead of hyprpolkitagent's. A session has one agent, so remove the other from your autostart first.

entries.title: Spotify listener stays up
entries.detail: Keep the lyrics listener running across shell reloads. Off restarts it with the shell.

entries.title: Move
entries.detail: API keys and the Discord client secret are kept in the system keyring when one is running (new keys go there on their own); otherwise in 0600 files, as before. Moving the keys already in files verifies each one before the file's copy is dropped, and may ask your wallet to unlock.

entries.title: Shell presets
entries.detail: Every settings page, saved under a name; tap one to apply it. To use it on another machine: commit presets/shell.json, git pull there, and tap it. Bar presets (presets/bar.json) and desktop-widget placement (widgets.json) are their own files. Commit them too if you want them.

entries.title: Preview
entries.detail: A card drawn at your settings, from the shell's real components. Everything on this page changes it.

entries.title: Text
entries.detail: The font for labels, titles and body copy everywhere in the shell.

entries.title: Numerals
entries.detail: The font for throughput, timers and other figures that must line up. A monospace face is best.

entries.title: Display
entries.detail: The font for the big clock on the lock and login screens. Heavier faces read best.

entries.title: Spacing
entries.detail: How tightly everything packs: padding, gaps, row heights.

entries.title: Roundness
entries.detail: Corner radius of cards, panels and controls. The bar and desktop widgets keep their own.

entries.title: Opacity
entries.detail: How much of the desktop shows through the shell's surfaces.

entries.title: High contrast
entries.detail: Stronger text and accent colours, solid borders and fully opaque surfaces. The opacity sliders keep their values for when you switch it off.

entries.title: Shadows
entries.detail: How far surfaces float. At zero the shell stops drawing shadows altogether.

entries.title: Reduced motion
entries.detail: Keeps fades and state changes, drops bounce, parallax, drifting shapes, the colour-change wave and idle spinning.

entries.title: Motion
entries.detail: Every animation in the shell (panels, notifications, the lock screen, the bar) runs through these two.

entries.title: Auto-hide
entries.detail: Rest the pointer on the edge, or press Super+D (by default), to bring it back.

entries.title: Dodge windows
entries.detail: A kind of auto-hide: the sidebar stays out until a window would sit under it.

entries.title: Empty workspaces
entries.detail: Nothing to cover and nothing else to look at, so the sidebar and its dock stay out until a window opens. (End-4's rule.)

entries.title: Edge reveal
entries.detail: Turn this off to stop the sidebar popping out whenever the pointer brushes the edge. Combine it with Empty workspaces and the dock's keep button.

entries.title: Edge & size
entries.detail: The bar owns the top edge; the sidebar takes one of the other three. Everything on it is sized around the dock's icons.

entries.title: Reserve space
entries.detail: Tiled windows leave the sidebar's edge free. Off while auto-hide is on, since it would reserve an empty strip.

entries.title: Mixer
entries.detail: Off until you turn it on. Every sound is generated on this machine (scripts/gen-sfx.py). Nothing is downloaded.

entries.title: Output
entries.detail: Where sound goes, and how loud. Click the speaker to mute; scroll over the level to step it.

entries.title: Input
entries.detail: What the machine can hear. Test plays your microphone back through the output, so you hear how you actually sound. Headphones only, or it howls.

entries.title: Applications
entries.detail: Per-app volume, and which device each one plays on. It is a PipeWire stream property, so it follows the app, not this page.

entries.title: Recording
entries.detail: Applications holding the microphone open.

entries.title: Disks
entries.detail: Each disk's used space against its size. The root disk is broken down by what fills it; Other is everything not measured on its own, and Reserved is the share the filesystem keeps for root, which is why the numbers seem not to add up.

entries.title: Reclaim space
entries.detail: Caches, old package versions and logs: files that rebuild themselves. Orphans are packages nothing needs any more; removing those uninstalls them, so it asks twice.

entries.title: Home folder
entries.detail: Each tile is a folder in your home, as large as its share of the space. Hover one for its path. Nothing here is ever deleted for you.

entries.title: Light touch
entries.detail: How hard you press before the pen starts to draw. Raise it to ignore a pen that just rests on the surface.

entries.title: Full press
entries.detail: The pressure that counts as all the way down. Lower it to reach full strokes with a lighter hand.

entries.title: Live pressure
entries.detail: What the pen reports right now, before the range above is applied.

entries.title: Read the tablet
entries.detail: The live pen and the express keys come from the tablet's input device, which only the system may open. This adds one udev rule that lets you, while you are logged in, and nothing else. It asks for your password once.

entries.title: Install
entries.detail: Official packages update together. Installing one on its own is a partial upgrade, which breaks programs that rely on the libraries left behind, so tick AUR and Flatpak ones to install them singly.

entries.title: Official
entries.detail: Official packages can't be ticked: installing one on its own is a partial upgrade. Hold skips a package on the next full upgrade (--ignore); Flatpak has no way to skip one.

entries.title: Recently changed
entries.detail: The tail of pacman's own log: what was upgraded, installed or removed, and when. After a run it is the receipt.

entries.title: Check for new versions
entries.detail: Asks GitHub every 6 hours for a newer signed release of the shell.

entries.title: Quicktest
entries.detail: Updates to the shell itself: signed releases from GitHub. Needs no password, the shell lives in your own config folder.

entries.title: Re-patch Vencord
entries.detail: Downloads the official VencordInstaller and runs it as root. Re-apply this after Discord updates itself and drops the patch.

entries.title: Release all
entries.detail: Skipped with --ignore on the next upgrade.

entries.title: Drawn by
entries.detail: Static images only.

entries.title: Depth
entries.detail: How far the clock stays behind when the picture moves, so it slides behind the subject. Needs parallax on.

entries.title: Edge softness
entries.detail: Blurs the edge where the subject covers the clock, so the pixels of the cut-out don't show.

entries.title: Apply images to
entries.detail: Scenes always cover every screen.

entries.title: Performance
entries.detail: Options apply on Refresh.

entries.title: Play scenes through the shell
entries.detail: On, each scene keeps using the GPU while it waits. Off, a scene's own parallax works only over a bare desktop.

entries.title: Monitors
entries.detail: One scene per screen, or one spanned across several.

entries.title: Library
entries.detail: Blank = the default folder.

entries.title: Music effects
entries.detail: Pictures, and Wallpaper Engine scenes the shell plays from a window (scene preload on). Rests while nothing plays, behind a fullscreen window and in Game Mode.

entries.title: Intensity
entries.detail: How strong everything is at its biggest. The song does the rest: calm parts settle to a soft glow, big parts move, the drop hits hardest, and a busy part (sixteenth hi-hats) plays smaller.

entries.title: Sync
entries.detail: The effects already wait for your speakers. If they still land before the beat you hear (Bluetooth adds more delay than it reports), hold them back further.

entries.title: Bar glow is set in Bar & islands › Style
Sound map
entries.detail: Every sound is on, and the song decides how much each one shows: little in a calm part, all of it in a big one, more on the drop. Slide one to want more or less of it; Auto puts every sound back. Strobe is never on unless you turn it on.

entries.title: Peak caps
entries.detail: A cap over each bar that holds, then falls

entries.title: Glow
entries.detail: A soft light round it, in its colour

entries.title: Album cover
entries.detail: The cover inside the ring while music plays

entries.title: Desktop visualiser
entries.detail: A live spectrum of what's playing, pinned behind your windows.

entries.title: Add a widget
entries.detail: Click one to place it

entries.title: Screen
entries.detail: The one the map shows

entries.title: On this screen
entries.detail: Pick one here or on the map to change its size and options, or drag it on the map to move it.

entries.title: Bring forward what matters
entries.detail: A running timer, or the music while something plays

entries.title: Mount point
entries.detail: A path from System › Storage: “/” or “/home”.

entries.title: Cities
entries.detail: Offsets are hours from UTC. A city that changes for daylight saving needs editing twice a year.

entries.title: Grow from centre
entries.detail: Bars extend both ways from the middle, like the bar pill

entries.title: Track card
entries.detail: What's playing, shown when a song starts and when you hover; plus how far through it is

entries.title: Soft edges
entries.detail: Lines fade out at the top and bottom instead of being cut

entries.title: Tile frame
entries.detail: The widget's own fill and outline, around the card

entries.title: Liquid glass
entries.detail: A graded fill, a lit rim and a sheen, instead of a plain translucent tile.

entries.title: Grow on hover
entries.detail: A widget swells a little under the pointer.

entries.title: Parallax tilt
entries.detail: A widget leans under the pointer and its contents shift the other way. Hover a widget on the map to see it. How far is Parallax strength, below.

entries.title: Entrance
entries.detail: Widgets pop in one after another when the desktop loads or one is added.

entries.title: Parallax strength
entries.detail: How far a widget leans and its contents shift under the pointer. Needs Parallax tilt on.

entries.title: Snap grid
entries.detail: Widgets you drag snap to this grid.

entries.title: Style
entries.detail: Every widget

entries.title: Weather location
entries.detail: Only the place you pick is ever requested. Your location is never looked up from your IP. Night light and the calendar use it too.

entries.title: Screen
entries.detail: Where a preset lands

entries.title: Layout presets
entries.detail: Click a preset to load it once, on the chosen screen. Right-click one to give the screen's wallpaper that preset LIVE instead: switch to the wallpaper and its tiles take over automatically; switch away and your normal ones return. Follows the colour scheme panel's own click-to-load / right-click-to-bind split.

entries.title: Calendars
entries.detail: Paste a calendar's .ics address (Google: your calendar's settings › Secret address in iCal format) and its events show in the clock panel, read-only, in a colour of their own. The address stays on this machine.
